title: Should ProofNotFluff pivot from selling data tools to selling done-for-you outcomes?
text:
WHO: ProofNotFluff (PNF), a one-person US business run by an owner whose background is corporate finance: FP&A at large consumer packaged goods companies, then VP Finance building e-commerce finance from zero at a consumer brand (Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, Target). He also runs two short-term rental homes. AI agents do most of the building; he holds every account and approves every send and spend. Spend is near $0 by rule. Goal: one $1,000 month, net of fees, by Jan 31, 2027.

WHAT PNF HAS TODAY (Oct 29, 2026):
- Website proofnotfluff.com: free calculators for trade owners (lead cost, cleaning price floor, bid calculator), 11 free Chicago public-data pages (permits, restaurant inspections, rat complaints, new business licenses), a daily Chicago trades news page. About 362 page views a week, almost none from search yet.
- Paid data products, all on monthly subscription: Chicago and Austin construction cleaning leads $29/month (new building permits near finish, for post-construction cleaners), Chicago restaurant inspection leads $39/month, a pest control seat $149/month (3 seats), area seats for cleaners $149/month (one company per area, 6 areas), new business licenses list $29/month.
- An outreach machine: two sending inboxes, cold email templates under 75 words with no links, email verification, a CRM, a pipeline of about 730 general contractor leads from permits and about 279 prospect businesses.
- A daily short-video engine (faceless animated host, AI voice) posting one lesson a day to TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube on how trade owners win and handle leads (after-hours replies, markup vs margin, turning notes into a quote).
- Older: $2.99 spreadsheet downloads on Etsy (0 orders), a $79 13-week cash flow kit for e-commerce brands (built, never published).
RESULTS SO FAR: 0 paying customers, 0 replies to about 57 cold emails (as of Oct 25), a few hundred views per video.

THE CLAIM TO TEST (a short-video reel citing a Sequoia partner): Software tools lose; sell the outcome instead. Businesses spend about $6 on services for every $1 on software. Pick a job businesses already pay humans for (bookkeeping, recruiting, content, paperwork), sell the result ("your books are closed on the 1st", "500 leads on your desk by Friday"), do the work with AI behind the curtain, look like an agency, charge what the outcome is worth. Stop selling the copilot, sell the autopilot.

DRAFT POSITION: PNF currently sells tools and lists (data the owner still has to act on), which may be why nobody pays. PNF should pivot to selling a done-for-you outcome.
question: Work from first principles, not the reel's framing. Use the four JSON fields this way. agree: which parts of the reel truly apply to PNF and why. disagree: which of the reel's assumptions are false or risky for a solo operator with these assets (consider the $6 to $1 figure, that one person can deliver agency results, that buyers do not care how, that outcomes always beat tools, and whether the real bottleneck is the offer or trust and distribution). missing: what the draft position ignores. top_three: your own three best outcome offers for PNF, ranked, each written as: outcome sold | who pays | price and why | which PNF assets it reuses | biggest risk | the cheapest test that would prove someone pays, using $0 spend. No invented statistics; where a number matters, say what you would check.
